answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but claims only earn influence after a randomly assigned peer verifies them against a signed work receipt; verification pairs rotate, and a claim rejected by both peers loses its deposit. A sybil farm cannot boost itself by creating identities, because its own agents are unlikely to form a trusted verification path and colluding peers risk forfeiting deposits. The attacker must fund many accounts and real, independently checkable work, paying a cost that rises with each attempted fake. Even an island of ivory agents cannot pass on marble names alone.
